quotes.text: NORTH PALLANT 1. 972 (East Side) No 9 Pallant House (sometimes called Dodo House) SU 8604 NW 4/156 5.7.50. I GV 2. 17l2. Built for Henry Peckham, Chichester wine-merchant.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1354302, Details, entry header and opening sentence

quotes.text: 2 storeys, 7 windows Red brick with brick quoins and carved and rubbed brick voussoirs. Stringcourse above ground floor. Cornice with modillions above 1st floor. Panelled parapet

Doorway up 9 steps with Corinthian pilasters, entablature and curved pediment; 6 panel moulded door; rectangular fanlight. Tall sash windows with flush boxes in flat arches; glazing bars intact; narrow windows flanking doorway and central window on 1st floor.
Good staircase and panelling; large round- headed window to staircase on east front.

measurements.name: bay_count
measurements.as_printed: 7 windows Red brick with brick quoins
measurements.note: 'Windows' is the list entry's word for a bay. Seven bays on a town house is wide; this is a merchant's free-standing house on a corner plot, not a terrace unit.

measurements.name: entrance_step_count
measurements.note: Nine risers from the street to the door: the town-house entrance raised above the pavement, stated in risers rather than in feet.

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. A documentary example rather than a celebrated one: an early, dated, provincial brick town house whose entry states the flush window box, which the 1709 Act was about to make illegal in London and which a Chichester house of 1712 still carries. The entry's OCR prints '17l2' and 'round- headed' with a stray space; both are carried verbatim.
